name: 2 Thessalonians
description: Endurance · relief · tested messages · quiet work · correction

1.text: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the assembly of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We are bound to always give thanks to God for you, brothers, even as it is appropriate, because your faith grows exceedingly, and the love of each and every one of you toward one another abounds,
so that we ourselves boast about you in the assemblies of God for your perseverance and faith in all your persecutions and in the afflictions which you endure.
This is an obvious sign of the righteous judgment of God, to the end that you may be counted worthy of God’s Kingdom, for which you also suffer.
For it is a righteous thing with God to repay affliction to those who afflict you,
and to give relief to you who are afflicted with us when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with his mighty angels in flaming fire,
punishing those who don’t know God, and to those who don’t obey the Good News of our Lord Jesus,
who will pay the penalty: eternal destruction from the face of the Lord and from the glory of his might,
when he comes in that day to be glorified in his saints and to be admired among all those who have believed, because our testimony to you was believed.
To this end we also pray always for you that our God may count you worthy of your calling, and fulfill every desire of goodness and work of faith with power,
that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.

2.text: Now, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering together to him, we ask you
not to be quickly shaken in your mind or troubled, either by spirit or by word or by letter as if from us, saying that the day of Christ has already come.
Let no one deceive you in any way. For it will not be unless the rebellion comes first, and the man of sin is revealed, the son of destruction.
He opposes and exalts himself against all that is called God or that is worshiped, so that he sits as God in the temple of God, setting himself up as God.
Don’t you remember that when I was still with you, I told you these things?
Now you know what is restraining him, to the end that he may be revealed in his own season.
For the mystery of lawlessness already works. Only there is one who restrains now, until he is taken out of the way.
Then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord will kill with the breath of his mouth and destroy by the manifestation of his coming;
even he whose coming is according to the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders,
and with all deception of wickedness for those who are being lost, because they didn’t receive the love of the truth, that they might be saved.
Because of this, God sends them a powerful delusion, that they should believe a lie,
that they all might be judged who didn’t believe the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.
But we are bound to always give thanks to God for you, brothers loved by the Lord, because God chose you from the beginning for salvation through sanctification of the Spirit and belief in the truth,
to which he called you through our Good News, for the obtaining of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So then, brothers, stand firm and hold the traditions which you were taught by us, whether by word or by letter.
Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who loved us and gave us eternal comfort and good hope through grace,
comfort your hearts and establish you in every good work and word.

3.text: Finally, brothers, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may spread rapidly and be glorified, even as also with you,
and that we may be delivered from unreasonable and evil men; for not all have faith.
But the Lord is faithful, who will establish you and guard you from the evil one.
We have confidence in the Lord concerning you, that you both do and will do the things we command.
May the Lord direct your hearts into God’s love and into the perseverance of Christ.
Now we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you withdraw yourselves from every brother who walks in rebellion and not after the tradition which they received from us.
For you know how you ought to imitate us. For we didn’t behave ourselves rebelliously among you,
neither did we eat bread from anyone’s hand without paying for it, but in labor and travail worked night and day, that we might not burden any of you.
This was not because we don’t have the right, but to make ourselves an example to you, that you should imitate us.
For even when we were with you, we commanded you this: “If anyone is not willing to work, don’t let him eat.”
For we hear of some who walk among you in rebellion, who don’t work at all, but are busybodies.
Now those who are that way, we command and exhort in the Lord Jesus Christ, that they work with quietness and eat their own bread.
But you, brothers, don’t be weary in doing what is right.
If any man doesn’t obey our word in this letter, note that man and have no company with him, to the end that he may be ashamed.
Don’t count him as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother.
Now may the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times in all ways. The Lord be with you all.
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand, which is the sign in every letter. This is how I write.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

chapters.title: Growing faith amid suffering leads into hope for relief and prayer for good work
chapters.summary: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy write again to the Thessalonians. They thank God that the readers’ faith grows and their love increases. They boast of the readers’ endurance in persecutions. They say God will repay the afflicters and give relief to the afflicted. That will happen when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with his angels. Those who do not obey the good news will be punished. He will be glorified in his saints on that day. The writers pray that God will count the readers worthy of their calling.
chapters.meaning: Verses 6–10 promise relief at the Lord’s revealing, which is still future. Verse 11 says what the writers ask for the time between. “To this end” ties the prayer to that day. They ask God to count the readers worthy of their calling. They ask him to complete every good desire and work of faith with power. The work is the readers’, and the power is God’s. Verse 12 gives the aim: the name of Jesus glorified in them.

lds.text: Why does promised relief lead into prayer for continued good work?

chapters.historicalNote: The shared greeting leads into thanks for growing faith and love amid continued suffering. The teachers treat endurance as reason for praise rather than proof that God abandoned them. Relief and repayment belong to the Lord's future judgment instead of the hearers' immediate control. The severe image of fire places that reversal beyond the present advantage of their persecutors. The prayer returns attention to good desires and work that God can bring to completion. Future judgment therefore supports continued faithful conduct rather than supplying a private task of revenge.

chapters.routeEvidence: The letter gives no delivery route.

chapters.title: Claims that the day has arrived must answer the instruction already received
chapters.summary: Paul asks them not to be shaken by a letter said to be his. Such a message says the day of the Lord has already come. That day will not come before the rebellion and the man of sin. That man will sit in God’s temple and claim to be God. Something now restrains him. The Lord Jesus will destroy him by the breath of his mouth. Those who refused to love the truth will be deceived. Paul thanks God for choosing the readers and tells them to stand firm.
chapters.meaning: Verse 2 names three ways a false report could come: spirit, word, or letter. Any of them might claim the writers’ authority. Verse 5 reminds them that Paul told them these things in person. Verse 15 gives the test that follows. They are to hold what the writers taught, by word or by letter. A new claim is measured against that teaching. Verse 3:17 adds a safeguard: Paul’s own handwriting marks every letter.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson applies falling away to the Great Apostasy before Christ's return. Why can a message claimed to come from the teachers still require testing?

chapters.historicalNote: The opening addresses alarm caused by a message claimed to come from the teachers. The hearers must not accept that claim simply because it invokes a spirit or letter. Rebellion and the self-exalting figure belong to the sequence offered against that alarming message. The restraining force remains unnamed because the speaker assumes knowledge not fully explained here. Signs and wonders cannot secure trust when they serve deception rather than love of truth. The ending directs the hearers toward received teaching, comfort, and good work instead of alarm.

chapters.title: Refusal of work calls for correction that still recognizes a brother
chapters.summary: Paul asks for prayer that the Lord’s word will spread quickly. The Lord is faithful and will guard them. He commands them to withdraw from any brother who refuses to work. He worked night and day and ate no one’s bread for free. He gave the rule that one who will not work should not eat. Some are busybodies and should work quietly. Anyone who ignores this letter should be noted and avoided. Paul signs with his own hand.
chapters.meaning: Verse 14 tells them to note a disobedient person and keep away. The stated aim is that he be ashamed. Verse 15 limits how far that goes. He is not to be counted an enemy. He is to be admonished, and the word used for him is still “brother.” Verse 6 used the same word at the start of the instruction. The distance is meant to correct him, not to disown him.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson teaches useful work for oneself and people in need. How does treating the person as a brother limit the aim of separation?

chapters.historicalNote: The request for prayer makes the teachers' work depend on support from the hearers. Their remembered labor then supplies an example for the present problem of refusal and interference. The food command addresses unwillingness to work rather than every condition that prevents work. Jennifer Wyant reads the passage within the group's problem of irresponsible work and meddling. Separation aims at correction, yet the ending still forbids treating the person as an enemy. The handwritten greeting answers the earlier concern about messages falsely claiming the teachers' authority.

people.name: Paul
people.role: Writer who corrects the Thessalonians and asks for prayer
people.relations: He writes with Silvanus and Timothy. He calls the readers brothers.
people.meaning: Paul thanks the Thessalonians for growing faith in suffering. He asks them not to be shaken by a letter said to come from him. He tells them to withdraw from brothers who will not work. He signs the greeting with his own hand as the sign in every letter.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Silvanus
people.role: Co-sender named with Paul and Timothy
people.relations: The letter names him first after Paul. Timothy follows him.
people.meaning: The letter names Silvanus in the opening line with Paul and Timothy. The letter says “we” after that. It says nothing else about him by name.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Timothy
people.role: Co-sender named with Paul and Silvanus
people.relations: The letter names him last, after Paul and Silvanus.
people.meaning: The letter names Timothy in the opening line with Paul and Silvanus. The letter says “we” after that. It says nothing else about him by name.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jesus Christ
people.role: Lord who will come, bring relief, and judge
people.relations: Paul calls him the Lord Jesus Christ. Paul links the readers’ calling and comfort with him.
people.meaning: Paul says the Lord Jesus will be revealed from heaven. He will give relief to the afflicted and punish those who do not obey. Some claim the day of Christ has already come. Paul answers that it has not, and he gives no date.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
